content.text:
The report is 7.4 MB uncompressed and 2.3 MB gzipped. About two-thirds of it is the test data embedded as JSON, and most of that is test guide text (`TestDescription`), repeated once for each of the 1,237 tests.

| Part | Size | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **Report data JSON** (`maester-report-data`) | **4.98 MB** | |
| ↳ `Tests[]` → `ResultDetail.TestDescription` | 1.96 MB | Each test's Markdown guide. 1.04 MB of it belongs to the 699 Skipped or NotRun tests, which nobody reads |
| ↳ `Tests[]` → `ResultDetail.TestResult` | 0.62 MB | The actual result Markdown. The biggest are ZTA.21770 (44 KB), MT.1024 (31 KB) and ZTA.21867 (30 KB) |
| ↳ `Tests[]` → other fields | 1.45 MB | Name, Title, ReasonDetail, ScriptBlockFile, Package, HelpUrl, Benchmark, Permission, Control and so on. Name and Title largely repeat each other |
| ↳ `AffectedObjects` | 0.44 MB | 614 objects. 139 of them aren't used by any test (`Referenced:false`, 25 KB) |
| ↳ `MaesterConfig.TestSettings` | 0.16 MB | 1,237 entries of Id, Title and Severity, which copy fields the tests already carry |
| ↳ Frameworks, Taxonomy, tenant info and the rest | 0.09 MB | |
| **Attachments** (stored gzipped, then base64-encoded) | **1.86 MB** | |
| ↳ `ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html` | 0.91 MB | The full ZTA report, 2.7 MB before compression. It has its own `window.reportData` inside, so it repeats what the ZTA tests already hold |
| ↳ `zero-trust-workshop` JSON | 0.95 MB | 2.3 MB before compression. A fixed catalogue that is the same on every run |
| **App code** (JS bundle, CSS, favicon) | **~0.55 MB** | |

By suite, the test data is ZTA 1.36 MB (327 tests), MT 0.82 MB, CIS 0.63 MB, CISA 0.28 MB, ORCA 0.15 MB, EIDSCA 0.13 MB and AZDO 0.13 MB. So the ZTA pack accounts for about 2.3 MB of the file once you add its two attachments.

These cuts would make the biggest difference, largest first:
1. **Don't embed `TestDescription` for Skipped/NotRun tests**, or store each guide once and look it up: saves about 1–2 MB.
2. **Stop embedding the workshop catalogue in every report**, since it never changes: about 0.95 MB.
3. **Drop the duplicate data in the embedded ZTA HTML report**, or link to it instead: up to about 0.9 MB.
4. **Remove the copy of Id/Title/Severity in `TestSettings`**, and the objects in `AffectedObjects` that no test uses: about 0.2 MB.

The sidecar files in the same folder are just as big: the `.md` is 7.9 MB and the `.json` 6.7 MB. They probably carry the same descriptions, so the same trimming would apply to them.
what will the new size be after trimming. will there be a change in functionality or will we pull them down from maester.dev in real time if the user opens that part of the static ocntent?

// Reports of other tools embedded with Add-MtReportAttachment. The report data lists each one; its content is
// gzip-compressed HTML, Base64-encoded, in a <script type="application/octet-stream"> element of its own.

export interface ReportAttachment {
  Id: string
  Name: string
  TestId?: string | null
  ContentType?: string
  FileName?: string | null
  Size?: number
}

const elementIdPrefix = "maester-attachment-"

function attachmentElement(attachment: ReportAttachment) {
  return document.getElementById(elementIdPrefix + attachment.Id)
}

// An attachment is a page (text/html, the default) or data a built-in view reads (application/json).
const isData = (attachment: ReportAttachment) => /json/i.test(attachment.ContentType || "")

/** The attached pages of a result whose content is in this page (the dev server and imported JSON have none). */
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
export function getReportAttachments(testResults: any): ReportAttachment[] {
  const attachments: ReportAttachment[] = Array.isArray(testResults?.Attachments) ? testResults.Attachments : []
  return attachments.filter((attachment) => attachment?.Id && attachment.Name && !isData(attachment) && attachmentElement(attachment))
}

/** The data attachment of this name, such as the Zero Trust plan, when its content is in this page. The dev
 * server's samples name theirs with an Id that starts with "dev:" and have no content element. */
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
export function getDataAttachment(testResults: any, name: string): ReportAttachment | undefined {
  const attachments: ReportAttachment[] = Array.isArray(testResults?.Attachments) ? testResults.Attachments : []
  return attachments.find((a) => a?.Id && a.Name === name && isData(a) && ((import.meta.env.DEV && a.Id.startsWith("dev:")) || attachmentElement(a)))
}

/** The report route that shows an attachment in the main panel. */
export function getAttachmentPath(attachment: ReportAttachment) {
  return `/reports/${encodeURIComponent(attachment.Id)}`
}

/** The attachment a /reports/<id> route names, or undefined. */
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
export function findReportAttachment(testResults: any, pathname: string): ReportAttachment | undefined {
  const match = /^/reports/([^/]+)$/.exec(pathname)
  if (!match) return undefined
  let id: string
  try {
    id = decodeURIComponent(match[1])
  } catch {
    // A mistyped or cut link names no attachment.
    return undefined
  }
  return getReportAttachments(testResults).find((attachment) => attachment.Id === id)
}

/** The attachments a test added, shown on that test's result and on each instance of a family. */
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
export function getTestAttachments(testResults: any, test: { Id?: string; ParentId?: string | null }): ReportAttachment[] {
  return getReportAttachments(testResults).filter(
    (attachment) => attachment.TestId && (attachment.TestId === test.Id || attachment.TestId === test.ParentId)
  )
}

const decoded = new Map<string, Promise<string>>()

/** The attachment's content as text, decompressed once and kept. */
export function decodeAttachment(attachment: ReportAttachment): Promise<string> {
  let html = decoded.get(attachment.Id)
  if (!html) {
    html = (async () => {
      const base64 = attachmentElement(attachment)?.textContent?.trim() ?? ""
      const compressed = await fetch(`data:application/gzip;base64,${base64}`)
      if (!compressed.body) throw new Error("The attachment is empty.")
      return await new Response(compressed.body.pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream("gzip"))).text()
    })()
    decoded.set(attachment.Id, html)
    html.catch(() => decoded.delete(attachment.Id))
  }
  return html

input.ask: Should I gzip the embedded report data?

content.text:
The report can go from 7.4 MB to about 3.4 MB with no change in what it does and no calls to maester.dev. I've re-measured the trims from my last answer, and my recommendation has changed: compression gets most of the saving, and deleting content is no longer worth it.

**Why compression is enough:** the two attachments are already stored gzipped (gzip-compressed, then base64-encoded). The 5 MB of test data isn't. The report already decompresses attachments in the browser (`decodeAttachment` in [reportAttachments.ts](report/src/lib/reportAttachments.ts) uses `DecompressionStream`), so the test data can be stored and read the same way.

| Option | Report size | Change in what the report does |
|---|---|---|
| Today | 7.40 MB | — |
| **Gzip the test data** (4.98 MB → 0.96 MB) | **~3.4 MB** | None. It all still works offline. It adds a few tens of milliseconds at load. |
| + also drop guides for Skipped/NotRun tests | ~3.1 MB | Opening a skipped test no longer shows what it checks or how to fix it. Once the data is compressed this saves only 0.32 MB, so I don't think it's worth it. |
| + also load the workshop catalogue from maester.dev | ~2.1 MB | The Zero Trust workshop view needs the internet (see below). |

**What shouldn't be trimmed:**
- **The embedded Zero Trust Assessment report (0.91 MB).** It's the ZeroTrustAssessment tool's own output, and 1.15 MB of it is that report's data. Cutting it would break the report.
- **The workshop catalogue (0.95 MB).** It's 1.76 MB of task text and 0.6 MB of icons before compression.

**Why I wouldn't load content from maester.dev when a section is opened:**
- It breaks offline and air-gapped use. Many people share these reports by email, attach them to tickets or keep them as audit evidence.
- When a report is opened from disk (`file://`), or in an email or SharePoint viewer, the request can be blocked: by missing CORS headers on our side, or by the viewer's security rules (CSP).
- Guides change between versions, so an old report would show today's text instead of the text that matched its run.
- Every time someone opened the report, it would contact maester.dev. That's a privacy question for a security tool.

The workshop catalogue is the only reasonable candidate for loading from maester.dev, and it would still need a fallback for offline use, which cancels the saving.

**Side effects of compressing:** the test data would no longer be readable or searchable in a text editor. Two things read the current `const testResults=` slot and would need updating together:
- the report's loader, [reportData.ts](report/src/lib/reportData.ts)
- the demo report builder, [build-demo-report.mjs:86](website/scripts/build-demo-report.mjs:86)

Any outside scripts that pull data out of the HTML would also break. The `.json` file written next to the report is the right thing for those scripts to read.
Yes, compress it
